description: Failure patterns for three-phase squirrel-cage induction motors, direct-on-line or inverter-fed, covering electrical, supply, insulation, rotor, bearing, alignment, thermal and inverter-specific modes.

roles.quantity: phase current unbalance (max deviation from mean)
stator insulation resistance to ground (online monitor or last test)
number of starts in the last hour
motor protection relay thermal trip / PTC trip state

patterns.title: Mechanical overload (driven load too high)
patterns.description: The driven load demands more torque than rated. Slip and current rise; speed sags; winding heats over minutes.
patterns.typical_progression: Seconds for current/speed; minutes for winding temperature; protection trips if sustained.

symptoms.note: Above nameplate FLA × service factor
Slip increases; small absolute drop on stiff supplies
Class F alarm typically 130–140 °C

loops.description: Higher slip raises torque until it matches the load: the motor settles at a lower speed and higher current.
Hotter copper has higher resistance, which raises I²R loss and heats it further (≈0.4 %/°C for copper).

propagation.note: Higher current causes more supply/bus voltage drop
Drive output current follows motor current; the drive's current limit feeds back as a speed reduction

discriminators.rule: Overload: current rises BEFORE supply voltage falls. Undervoltage: voltage falls first and current rises in response.
Overload keeps phase currents balanced; single phasing shows current unbalance > 10 % and one phase near zero.
Overload has no rise in bearing envelope or bearing temperature ahead of current.

checks.text: Compare motor current with nameplate FLA × service factor; check it tracks process demand (flow, pressure, conveyor load).
Check the driven equipment for binding, blockage, over-pressure or product build-up.
Inspect the coupling and belts for tightness or damage.
Verify the protection relay thermal model / overload setting matches the nameplate.

patterns.title: Locked rotor / stall
patterns.description: The rotor cannot turn (seized load, jammed driven machine, or failed bearing). Current sits at locked-rotor level (5–8× FLA) and winding temperature climbs within seconds.
patterns.typical_progression: Seconds. Protection must trip within the locked-rotor safe time (typically 10–20 s hot).

symptoms.note: Locked-rotor current, 5–8× FLA across the line; drive-limited on a VFD
Near-zero speed while energised

propagation.note: Deep voltage dip from locked-rotor current

discriminators.rule: Stall: speed near zero within 2 s and current at LRA. Overload: speed only a few % lower and current 1.1–1.5× FLA.

checks.text: Confirm the protection tripped. If it did not, trip the motor locally at once; locked-rotor damage accrues in seconds.
Lock out, then try to rotate the shaft by hand to separate a seized motor from a jammed load.
Inspect the driven machine for a jam or foreign object.
Check the bearings for seizure before restarting.

patterns.title: Single phasing (loss of one phase)
patterns.description: One supply phase is open: a blown fuse, failed contactor pole or loose terminal. The motor keeps running on two phases with sharply unbalanced current and fast heating; it may not restart.
patterns.typical_progression: Seconds to minutes. Negative-sequence current heats the rotor quickly.

symptoms.note: Typically > 50 %; one phase near zero
Remaining phases carry ~1.7× current at the same load
Pulsating torque at 2× line frequency

propagation.note: Open phase appears as voltage unbalance at the motor terminals

discriminators.rule: Single phasing: one phase current near zero and unbalance > 30 %. Supply unbalance: all phases carry current; current unbalance is 6–10× the voltage unbalance.
Inter-turn short: unbalance grows gradually with a hot spot; single phasing is a step change.

checks.text: Check each phase current at the starter. One phase near zero confirms an open phase.
Inspect fuses, contactor poles and terminal lugs for an open circuit or burn marks.
Check upstream protection for a single-pole trip.
Do not restart until the open phase is found; a restart on two phases will stall.

patterns.title: Supply voltage unbalance
patterns.description: Unequal line voltages drive negative-sequence currents. Current unbalance is roughly 6–10× the voltage unbalance, causing extra rotor and stator heating.
patterns.typical_progression: Continuous. NEMA derates motors above 1 % unbalance; 5 % is a limit.

discriminators.rule: Supply unbalance: voltage unbalance comes first and follows the supply (other motors on the same bus see it). Inter-turn short: current unbalance without voltage unbalance.

checks.text: Measure all three line voltages at the motor terminals and at the bus. If other motors on the same bus show the same unbalance, the cause is upstream.
Check for large single-phase loads on the same transformer and for a failed PF-correction capacitor stage.
Derate the motor per the NEMA MG-1 derating curve until corrected.

patterns.title: Supply undervoltage
patterns.description: Low supply voltage cuts torque (∝ V²). To carry the same load the motor slips more and draws more current, so it heats even though the load is unchanged.

discriminators.rule: Undervoltage: voltage falls before current rises. Overload: current rises first.

checks.text: Check the bus / transformer voltage and tap setting; check for other large loads starting.
Check for voltage drop across long cable runs or undersized cables.

patterns.title: Supply overvoltage
patterns.description: High voltage drives magnetising current up (core saturation). Iron loss and no-load current rise and power factor drops.

symptoms.note: Magnetising component; most visible at light load

checks.text: Check transformer taps and PF-correction capacitors at light load.
Check the voltage regulator / generator AVR.

patterns.title: Stator inter-turn short circuit
patterns.description: Insulation between turns of one coil has failed. A circulating current in the shorted turns creates a local hot spot that quickly spreads into a phase-to-phase or phase-to-ground fault.
patterns.typical_progression: Minutes to hours from first detectable unbalance to a ground fault.

symptoms.note: Rising unbalance WITHOUT matching voltage unbalance
Local hot spot; an RTD in the affected slot reads high
The fault has escalated to ground

loops.description: The hot spot degrades neighbouring insulation, which shorts more turns and makes more heat.

discriminators.rule: The short shows current unbalance with balanced voltages; supply unbalance shows both.
Broken bars give (1±2s)·f sidebands and speed-dependent current pulsation, not a steady phase unbalance.

signatures.description: Negative-sequence current and 3rd-harmonic components rise; Park's vector pattern turns elliptical.

checks.text: Compare line-voltage unbalance with current unbalance. Balanced voltages with unbalanced currents point inside the motor.
Plan a controlled stop; run surge (turn-to-turn) and insulation resistance / polarization index tests.
Check the winding RTDs for a single hot phase.

patterns.title: Insulation degradation / ground fault
patterns.description: Stator insulation to ground has degraded from moisture, contamination, thermal ageing or voltage stress, leading to leakage and then a ground fault.
patterns.typical_progression: Weeks of IR decline (often seasonal or moisture-linked), then a sudden ground fault.

symptoms.note: IEEE 43 minimum ≈ (kV + 1) MΩ; a trend drop > 50 % is significant

checks.text: Megger test and polarization index (PI < 2 suggests moisture or contamination).
Check anti-condensation heaters, enclosure IP rating, and cable gland / terminal box seals.
Trend IR against ambient humidity; dry out the winding before a restart if it is wet.

patterns.title: Broken rotor bars / cracked end ring
patterns.description: A cracked or broken cage bar breaks rotor symmetry. Torque and current pulsate at twice slip frequency; the cage near the break overheats and more bars crack.
patterns.typical_progression: Weeks to months; accelerated by frequent heavy starts.

symptoms.note: Current and power beat at 2·s·f (visible as needle swing on an ammeter)
With 2·s·f / pole-pass sidebands

nodes.label: Adjacent bars carry more current and heat

loops.description: Neighbouring bars take over the broken bar's current, overheat and crack in turn.

discriminators.rule: Broken bars give sidebands at (1±2s)·f around the supply line. Eccentricity gives components at f ± fr (rotation-frequency sidebands).

signatures.description: Motor current signature analysis: lower sideband amplitude relative to the fundamental. > −45 dB watch; > −35 dB several broken bars.

checks.text: Run motor current signature analysis at > 50 % load, where slip-dependent sidebands resolve best.
Trend the sideband amplitude over time; one reading is not conclusive.
At the next outage, run a single-phase rotation test or a growler test on the rotor.

references: Thomson & Fenger, 'Current signature analysis to detect induction motor faults', IEEE IAS Magazine 2001

patterns.title: Air-gap eccentricity (static / dynamic)
patterns.description: The rotor is not centred in the stator bore, from worn bearings, a bent shaft or a misaligned end shield. This gives unbalanced magnetic pull, 2×LF vibration and, in the extreme, rotor-to-stator rub.

symptoms.note: Dynamic eccentricity modulates at 1×

discriminators.rule: Eccentricity vibration is at 2×LF and disappears the instant power is cut. Unbalance vibration is at 1× and coasts down with speed.

signatures.description: A 2×line-frequency peak that disappears immediately on de-energising (electrical origin)

checks.text: Take a power-off coast-down vibration reading. An instant drop of the 2×LF peak confirms an electromagnetic cause.
Measure the air gap at four points per end (outage).
Check the bearings and end-shield fits.

patterns.title: Rolling-element bearing defect
patterns.description: Race or rolling-element damage from fatigue, contamination or electrical fluting. The first sign is high-frequency envelope energy; overall vibration and bearing temperature rise late.
patterns.typical_progression: Weeks to months (P-F interval). Envelope rises first, then 1× harmonics, then temperature, then failure.

symptoms.note: gE alarm; set per speed and bearing size
Late indicator; ~20 °C above baseline is significant
Only at advanced friction

loops.description: Heat thins the lubricant, which raises friction and heat further.

discriminators.rule: Lubrication failure raises temperature and broadband noise with no discrete defect frequencies; a defect shows BPFO/BPFI peaks in the envelope spectrum.
Fluting shows washboard marks and BPFO-like peaks, plus high shaft voltage on VFD-fed motors.

checks.text: Take an envelope spectrum; match peaks to the bearing's BPFO/BPFI/BSF/FTF for the installed bearing number.
Check the lubrication schedule and grease type/quantity (over-greasing also causes heat).
Plan a replacement inside the P-F interval; trend weekly.

patterns.title: Bearing lubrication failure
patterns.description: Too little, too much, degraded or wrong grease. The oil film breaks down: friction, temperature and broadband high-frequency noise rise.

symptoms.note: Broadband 'carpet' rather than discrete peaks

checks.text: Check the last re-greasing date and quantity against the manufacturer interval.
Check for grease purging, discoloured grease or mixed incompatible greases.
After re-greasing, confirm temperature and envelope fall within an hour. If they do not, suspect bearing damage.

patterns.title: Shaft misalignment (motor ↔ driven machine)
patterns.description: Angular or parallel offset between the motor and driven shafts loads the bearings and coupling. It shows as axial vibration and 2× components.

symptoms.note: Axial > 50 % of radial suggests angular misalignment

propagation.note: The misaligned coupling loads both machines' bearings

discriminators.rule: Unbalance is dominated by radial 1× with a 90° phase shift between horizontal and vertical. Misalignment shows high axial vibration and 2×, with a 180° phase shift across the coupling.

signatures.description: High 1× and 2× (sometimes 3×) with strong axial components; 180° phase across the coupling

checks.text: Laser-align within the coupling manufacturer's tolerance at operating temperature (thermal growth).
Check for soft foot before aligning.
Check for pipe strain on the driven machine.

patterns.title: Rotor / coupling unbalance
patterns.description: Mass unbalance on the rotor, fan or coupling from build-up, erosion, a lost balance weight or a keyway mismatch. The force is at 1× running speed and grows with speed squared.

symptoms.note: ISO 20816-3 zone B/C boundary for many machine groups

signatures.description: Dominant radial 1×; horizontal and vertical ~90° apart; amplitude ∝ speed²

checks.text: Check the phase reading at 1× in horizontal and vertical (≈90° apart confirms unbalance).
Inspect the fan and coupling for build-up or damage; confirm key length matches (half-key convention).
Field-balance in one or two planes.

patterns.title: Mechanical looseness / soft foot
patterns.description: Loose hold-down bolts, a cracked base or soft foot distorts the frame. Vibration shows many harmonics of running speed and changes when bolts are loosened.

symptoms.note: Multiple harmonics, possibly ½× sub-harmonics
Soft foot distorts the stator and raises 2×LF

checks.text: Check each foot for soft foot with a dial indicator (> 0.05 mm is a soft foot).
Torque the hold-down bolts; inspect the base and grout for cracks.

patterns.title: Coupling wear / belt slip
patterns.description: A worn flexible element or slipping belt transmits less of the motor's speed. Motor speed stays up while driven speed and process output fall; belts heat and squeal.

symptoms.note: Less load transmitted
Motor speeds up slightly as load drops

propagation.note: Driven machine slows while the motor does not

discriminators.rule: Belt slip lowers motor current while driven output falls. Overload raises motor current.

checks.text: Compare motor speed with driven-machine speed (the slip ratio).
Check belt tension and wear, and the coupling element.

patterns.title: Cooling failure (blocked fan / fins / high ambient)
patterns.description: The TEFC fan is damaged, the fan cowl or fins are clogged, or the cooling air is too hot. Temperatures rise at normal current.

symptoms.note: Only when the cause is ambient

discriminators.rule: Cooling failure: temperature rises with NORMAL current. Overload: current rises first.

checks.text: Compare winding temperature rise (winding minus ambient) with current. A high rise at normal current points to cooling.
Inspect the fan and cowl, and clean the fins and air path.
On a VFD at low speed, the shaft-mounted fan loses airflow. Check the minimum-speed derating or a forced-vent blower.

patterns.title: Winding thermal runaway (sustained overtemperature)
patterns.description: The winding is above its insulation class limit and the reinforcing loop (temperature → resistance → loss) outpaces cooling. Insulation life halves for every ~10 °C above rating (Arrhenius).

symptoms.note: Class F limit 155 °C; class H 180 °C
Small rise as resistance and slip increase

loops.description: Copper resistance rises ≈0.39 %/°C, raising loss at the same current.
Heat removal rises with temperature difference; runaway happens when the reinforcing gain exceeds it.

checks.text: Reduce load immediately. Confirm the protection thermal model and PTC/RTD trips are active.
Identify the driver: overload, cooling, supply unbalance or duty cycle (see the linked patterns).
Record time above the class limit for insulation-life accounting.

patterns.title: Excessive starts / thermal cycling
patterns.description: Starting more often than the motor's permitted starts per hour. Each start dissipates roughly the rotor's stored kinetic energy as heat.

symptoms.note: Typical limit is 2 cold / 1 hot consecutive starts; check NEMA MG-1 12.54

checks.text: Check the control logic for short-cycling (level or pressure switch deadband too small).
Consider a soft starter or VFD, or widen the control deadband.

patterns.title: Inverter-fed harmonic heating
patterns.description: PWM voltage harmonics add rotor and stator losses (typically 5–15 %), and cooling falls at low speed. Temperature runs higher than on a sine supply at the same load.

symptoms.note: Worse at low output frequency (reduced self-cooling)

checks.text: Check the drive's switching frequency and output filter (dv/dt or sine filter).
Confirm the motor is inverter-duty rated (IEC 60034-17/-25, NEMA MG-1 Part 31) and apply the low-speed torque derating.

patterns.title: Inverter-induced bearing currents (EDM fluting)
patterns.description: Common-mode voltage from the PWM drive couples onto the shaft and discharges through the bearing oil film. This etches a washboard (fluting) pattern and bearing noise follows.
patterns.typical_progression: Months. Often shows 3–12 months after a VFD retrofit.

symptoms.note: Peak discharge voltage; > 10–15 V peak is a concern

signatures.description: Envelope peaks near BPFO with a 'washboard' broadband hump; the grease turns black and burnt

checks.text: Measure shaft-to-frame voltage with a brush probe while running on the VFD.
Inspect the removed bearing for frosting or fluting.
Mitigate with a shaft grounding ring, an insulated NDE bearing, symmetrical shielded VFD cable and correct high-frequency bonding.

patterns.title: Structural resonance
patterns.description: Running speed, or one of its harmonics, sits on a natural frequency of the base or structure. Vibration is very sensitive to speed, which is common on VFD-driven machines.

symptoms.note: A narrow speed band triggers it

checks.text: Run a speed sweep or bump test to find the natural frequency.
Program the drive's skip-frequency band around the resonance; stiffen the base if needed.
